title: Granite Pharma savings exploratory scenarios v0.3
content:
One-line summary: exploratory before/after cost model for Granite Pharma (chat + embeddings-heavy pipeline). This sheet models three scenarios (conservative, expected, aggressive) for Redwood Optimize recommendations: batching, prefix/KV caching, cheaper model routing for low-complexity queries, and 4-bit quantization for embedding generation.

Scope and constraints:
- Customer: Granite Pharma (internal alias: GRAN-PHARMA).
- Workload: clinical-document ingestion + conversational Q&A for internal R&D teams.
- Visible traffic: 12M tokens/month generation, 2.4M embedding vectors/month (text-embedding-ada style units equivalent).
- SLA: soft 200ms median generation latency requirement for interactive users; background embedding ingestion can be batched to tolerate minutes of delay.
- Data controls: PHI-sensitive, must remain in Dedicated or Private. Recommendations assume Dedicated with access to Redwood Optimize control plane.

High-level assumptions (input knobs):
- Generation cost per token current (on their dedicated pool): $0.00045/token (mixed of large models).
- Embedding cost current: $0.0012/vector.
- Average generation tokens per request: 350 tokens.
- Monthly requests (chat): 34k interactive sessions.
- Acceptable model swap: 30% of queries are low-complexity (FAQ/lookup) and can be routed to a cheaper 15B variant with comparable answer quality for Granite.
- KV cache effective hit rate after deploy: 18% of tokens avoided on average for repeated prefixes across the session distribution.
- Batching improvements (server-side): 22% token-cost reduction where batching applies (mainly embeddings ingestion and some background re-rank jobs).
- Quantization uplift: 4-bit quantization applied to embedding model yields 55% unit-cost reduction for embeddings (conservative assumes 45% if conversion friction occurs).

Baseline (current month) — raw numbers:
- Generation tokens/month: 12,000,000 tokens @ $0.00045/token = $5,400.00
- Embeddings/month: 2,400,000 vectors @ $0.0012/vector = $2,880.00
- Other infra costs (network, storage, ops): estimated fixed monthly add-on = $1,200.00
- Total baseline monthly = $9,480.00

Scenario models (monthly projections)
Table: Metric | Baseline | Conservative | Expected | Aggressive
- Total generation cost | $5,400 | $4,590 | $3,780 | $3,240
- Total embeddings cost | $2,880 | $1,980 | $1,296 | $1,080
- Infra/ops | $1,200 | $1,200 | $1,200 | $1,200
- Total monthly cost | $9,480 | $7,770 | $6,276 | $5,520
- Absolute savings vs baseline | $0 | $1,710 | $3,204 | $3,960
- % savings vs baseline | 0% | 18.0% | 33.8% | 41.8%

How we derived the scenario numbers (calculation notes):
- Conservative scenario assumptions: 10% model routing to cheaper variant; KV cache 10% effective; batching gains applied 12% to applicable workload; quantization takes 45% reduction for embeddings.
- Expected scenario assumptions: 30% model routing; KV cache 18% effective (as above); batching gains 22%; quantization 55% reduction for embeddings.
- Aggressive scenario assumptions: 45% model routing; KV cache 25% effective; batching 30% applied; quantization 60% reduction (best-case specialized pipeline).

Breakdown example (expected scenario math):
- Generation cost: start $5,400. Benefits: 30% of queries routed to cheaper model; cheaper model costs 40% of baseline per-token cost => effective generation cost multiplier = 0.7*1.0 + 0.3*0.4 = 0.82 => $5,400 * 0.82 = $4,428. Then apply KV cache token avoidance 18% of tokens => effective billed tokens drop to 82% => $4,428 * 0.82 = $3,630. Apply server-side batching benefits for the remaining 78% of tokens where batching helps (we conservatively estimate batching applies to 60% of remaining gen tokens) — we apply 22% cost reduction to that portion resulting in further $150 reduction (detailed workbook available). Final rounded generation cost shown in table = $3,780 (small buffer left for conversion variance).
- Embeddings: baseline $2,880. With quantization (55% reduction) => $1,296. With additional batching (where embeddings ingestion can be queued and batch-encoded) and caching for deduplication we estimate another 5% reduction baked into scenario.

Sensitivity checks (quick):
- If KV cache underperforms (only 7% hit rate), expected savings drop by ~6% absolute.
- If customer cannot accept model swap >15%, expected scenario drops to ~22% savings instead of 33.8% (approx).
- If embedding quantization conversion fails for compliance, embedding savings revert to baseline and total savings drop by ~30–35% of projected optimize savings.

Qualitative observations from initial calls:
- GRAN-PHARMA engineering prefers conservative deployment: they want canary first on internal R&D namespace with cold-start metrics observed for 2 weeks. They flagged regulatory documentation requirement for quantized weights (auditability).
- Their embedding pipeline has a lot of duplicated content (clinical forms repeated across batches) — high opportunity for dedupe + pre-cache.

Risk register (short):
- Quality regression risk: medium. Mitigation: A/B with holdout prompt set (200 golden prompts) and automatic rollback on any >3% drop in downstream label accuracy.
- Compliance/legal: requires KMS-backed artifact signing for quantized weights. Action: solutions eng to prepare PKI plan.
- Ops/observability gap: missing token-level cost attribution in their dedicated pool. Action: Redwood console instrument per-route token tagging and send initial 30-day telemetry export.

Recommended rollout plan (phased, with owners and target dates):
1) Discovery / measurement (2 weeks) — owner: Luis Ortega. Tasks: export last 30 days of token-level telemetry, identify top 15 repeated prefixes, snapshot current model latencies.
2) Canary routing + KV cache pilot (3 weeks) — owner: Maya Patel. Tasks: enable 10% routing to cheaper variant, enable KV cache for internal namespace, collect quality metrics.
3) Embedding quantization pilot (4 weeks) — owner: Hannah Greene + Solutions Eng. Tasks: produce quantized artifact under HSM/KMS, run validation against golden embedding recall sets.
4) Scale and automate (4–6 weeks) — owner: Product-Optimize PM. Tasks: autoscale policies, rollout policies, cost dashboards, documentation for audit.

Action items (immediate):
- Send JIRA ticket to infra for dedicated pool snapshot (JIRA: JIRA-OPT-678).
- Prep evaluation prompt set (owner: Maya) and schedule kickoff 2025-03-10.
- Share this sheet with GRAN-PHARMA lead (cc: compliance) and propose pilot start 2025-03-17.

Appendix: quick CSV-style cost table (expected scenario, monthly)

Notes on divergence between table and CSV: the sheet intentionally keeps a small engineering/quality buffer (~5–8%) in displayed scenario totals to reflect conversion friction (deployment time, minor config mismatches). The detailed workbook (linked_artifacts) has cell-level formulas and week-by-week ramp modeling.

Bottom line (one paragraph): if Granite Pharma accepts Redwood Optimize pilots (10–30% routing + KV cache + embedding quantization) and runs the recommended canary cadence, we estimate a realistic expected savings of ~33% monthly (~$3.2k/month) with an aggressive upside approaching ~42% if routing and cache hit rates are high and quantization deployment is smooth. Short-term priority: validate quality on golden prompts and get KMS/PKI sign-off for quantized artifacts.

Document history: v0.1 initial draft (2025-02-14), v0.2 added sensitivity checks (2025-02-21), v0.3 updated numbers after engineering call (2025-03-05).
